card.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea exchange accusations of aggression at the UN amid fears of regional war

pages.text: Ethiopia and Eritrea have exchanged accusations of aggression at the United Nations, raising fears of a new conflict in the Horn of Africa as fighting intensifies in Ethiopia’s northern Tigray region. The diplomatic spat follows allegations that Eritrean troops have crossed the border into Ethiopia to support rebels fighting the Ethiopian government. On October 9, 2026, Ethiopia told the UN Security Council that Eritrean troops had advanced as far as 60km (37 miles) into Tigray, accusing its neighbor of violating its sovereignty. Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos described the alleged incursion in a letter to the UN as a “blatant act of aggression” and invoked Article 51 of the UN Charter, which recognizes a country’s right to self-defense, though he did not specify what measures Ethiopia was taking. Eritrea rejected these accusations, calling them a pretext for an offensive by Addis Ababa. In a letter to the UN Security Council on October 10, 2026, Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh urged the body to condemn Ethiopia’s “deplorable declaration of war” and take “deterrent measures,” warning that an Ethiopian offensive would cause “huge devastation to the peoples of both countries and destabilise the whole region.”

The escalation follows a period of deteriorating relations between the two neighbors, who were allies during the 2020-2022 Tigray war but have since been at loggerheads over the 2022 peace agreement and Ethiopia’s demands for access to the Red Sea. On October 5, 2026, when Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed was sworn in for another five years, he stated that access to the sea was a priority, fueling speculation that he intends to take Eritrea's strategic port of Assab by force. While the Ethiopian government has ruled out the use of force to pursue sea access, Eritrea has viewed the claim as an affront. Current fighting in Tigray involves the Ethiopian government against a coalition of seven rebel groups, spearheaded by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). This coalition includes groups such as the Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM), the Afar Revolutionary Democratic Unity Front (ARDUF), and the Oromo Liberation Army. Eritrea has used proxy politics—fostering armed groups inside Ethiopia to offset its relative limitations—to influence the region. Various sources have confirmed the presence of Eritrean armed forces in Ethiopia, with an AFP report quoting a foreign security source estimating that between 5,000 and 8,000 Eritrean soldiers were present in Tigray.

results.sourceTitle: Saudis probe how defense systems failed to stop deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh airport

card.headline: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport kill 13 and wound hundreds

pages.text: Multiple strikes launched by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 on October 10, 2026. The attacks, which the Houthi movement has claimed responsibility for, caused widespread disruption to air travel and left the airport shut. Video of the October 10 attack showed a packed airport before an explosion sent people running for safety as debris fell. A subsequent attack on December 6, 2026, killed one person and injured nearly a dozen others, according to Saudi reporting. The victims of the October 10 strikes included one American, four Saudi Arabian citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Palestinian, a Syrian, and one Sudanese national. The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia later stated that an Indian national injured in the October 10 attack had died. Adam Baron, a fellow at the Washington, D.C.-based think tank New America, described the situation as being on a ``strong escalation ladder.''

The attacks impacted the WPC Energy Congress, held in the Saudi capital near the airport. While Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman opened a session of the gathering by stating the country is safe, he added that the gathering does not mean the risk is gone. Several top energy executives, including the chief executives of Exxon Mobil, TotalEnergies, Shell, Chevron, and BP, were expected at the event starting October 11, 2026, but were no longer on the agenda released by organizers. In response to the strikes, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Egypt issued a joint statement through the R4 grouping holding the Houthis responsible and calling for an immediate stop to the attacks. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced on December 7, 2026, that his government would submit the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence to the Turkish parliament. Signed on August 7, the pact between Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three countries is to be treated as an attack against all. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has stated that Türkiye is assessing how to assist Saudi Arabia but has ruled out sending troops or participating in offensive operations, suggesting support would focus on defensive and technical capabilities.

results.sourceTitle: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says

card.headline: Russia strikes six Ukrainian energy facilities following Trump's announced energy ceasefire

pages.text: Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities on October 11, 2026, hours after US President Donald Trump announced that both Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes, which included hits on gas stations and energy infrastructure, suggested Russia was unwilling to accept the truce. Zelenskyy reported that 33 people were injured in the strikes across the country. He told Fox News that Ukraine did not attack Russia, while Russia attacked Ukrainian facilities, adding, “I think it was Putin's answer to President Trump.”

The strikes caused significant disruption to Ukraine's power supply. Ukraine's state-owned grid operator, Ukrenergo, reported new power cuts in Kharkiv, Donetsk, and Zaporizhzhia due to damage to energy equipment. In the city of Izyum, Russian strikes destroyed power grids, according to Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform. Additionally, energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine were targeted overnight. To prevent overloading damaged equipment, Ukrenergo has introduced electricity rationing in parts of the country. Zelenskyy stated on X that the strikes were proof Russia was unwilling to accept the ceasefire.

President Trump announced on October 11, 2026, that the energy ceasefire—a proposed arrangement designed to spare energy-related infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine—would be “effective immediately,” though he offered no specific details about the arrangement. This proposal follows Trump's October 9, 2026, announcement of a plan to import Russian diesel into the US. While Zelenskyy said he supports the concept of an energy ceasefire, he called for more pressure on Russia to ensure de-escalation succeeds. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov rejected the idea of a respite, stating that Ukraine does not deserve it and suggesting the proposal was an attempt by Zelenskyy to regroup and rearm.

results.sourceTitle: Iran sets crosshairs on ‘US-UAE’ oil shuttle out of Strait of Hormuz | US-Israel war on Iran News

card.headline: Iran targets US-UAE oil shuttle system in Strait of Hormuz

pages.text: Iranian authorities have declared a maritime shuttle system used to export energy through the Strait of Hormuz an explicit target for military action. Mohsen Rezaei, Iran's security chief, stated on the night of October 11, 2026, that the system is now a clear target for Tehran. The shuttle operation, which involves transferring oil from smaller vessels to larger tankers, is allegedly assisted by the United States military and the United Arab Emirates military to move crude oil despite a US naval blockade of Iran's southern ports and tightening sanctions. Rezaei claimed that Iran has been striking five or six participating vessels nightly for several weeks, asserting that while others are smuggling, the strait remains under Iranian control and management. The Strait of Hormuz is a strategic waterway that, prior to the current conflict, saw approximately one-fifth of global oil and gas flow through it. The waterway has been largely closed to shipping following Iranian attacks that began after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28. While the US Navy has reportedly opened a route to allow Gulf states to export oil and other commodities during the energy crisis, Iran has signaled it will use military and diplomatic pressure to force Washington to meet its demands regarding the reopening of the strait.

results.sourceTitle: Kremlin rejects Ukraine’s offer of a 60-day truce and presidential elections – The Irish Times

card.headline: Kremlin rejects Ukraine's proposal for 60-day truce and presidential elections

pages.text: The Kremlin has rejected a proposal from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for a 60-day truce and the holding of presidential elections. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that Moscow would only be willing to halt attacks for one day to allow Ukraine to hold elections, alleging that a 60-day ceasefire would be used by Ukraine to regroup and continue the war. Peskov also noted that President Vladimir Putin and other officials have repeatedly stated they do not want a ceasefire, though they seek long-term peace. This rejection follows a period of tension regarding a purported “energy ceasefire” announced by US President Donald Trump on October 11, 2026. While Trump claimed on Truth Social that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate energy ceasefire—an agreement intended to prevent strikes on energy systems—Zelenskyy stated that Kyiv was blindsided by the announcement and had not been consulted. Zelenskyy reported that Russia launched targeted strikes using drones and missiles against at least six energy targets, including a gas facility and a petrol station, immediately after Trump's post. Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready to respect an energy ceasefire if Russia does the same and is willing to sign guarantees as proof of commitment, but he noted that Russia's continued attacks suggest they have no interest in the agreement.

The dispute over the energy ceasefire comes amid shifting US policy and volatile global fuel markets. On October 9, 2026, President Trump struck a deal with Vladimir Putin for Russia to release more diesel, an announcement that followed his efforts to drive down fuel prices in the US ahead of November's midterm elections. Although European diesel prices fell in response to these efforts, Zelenskyy has criticized the deal as a reversal of Western policies aimed at isolating Russia's economy. The conflict has caused diesel prices—a critical fuel for agriculture and industry—to soar due to infrastructure damage from wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. In addition to the ceasefire dispute, President Trump has called on Ukrainians to unseat Zelenskyy in an election, suggesting on October 10, 2026, that Ukraine needs a new president. Irish Minister for Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee described these comments as concerning, and EU foreign ministers have met in Luxembourg to discuss the escalating dispute between the Trump administration and Ukraine.

results.sourceTitle: Iran warns of wider risks as regional attacks intensify | Iran International

card.headline: Two commercial vessels attacked near Oman and drone strike in Iraq as Iran warns of regional risks

pages.text: Two commercial vessels were attacked on October 11, 2026, near Oman, leaving two Indian sailors missing, while a drone struck an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region. These incidents occurred as Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, warned that a renewed war could put regional infrastructure within range of attack. Rezaei specifically threatened US-linked cables, data centers, and artificial intelligence facilities in the United Arab Emirates and around the Strait of Hormuz, warning that digital infrastructure could be targeted. He also promised a harsh response if Iran’s own energy and civilian infrastructure were attacked again.

Regarding the maritime attacks, India’s shipping minister reported that the Nicaragua-flagged Petro Dolphin was hit by a drone at the Sohar anchorage off Oman. While nine of the vessel's 11 Indian crew members were rescued, two remain missing. Separately, India’s foreign ministry stated that the Marshall Islands-flagged Valthera was struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, which caused a fire onboard; all 11 Indian crew members on that vessel were reported safe. India’s ministry condemned the attacks, and its embassy in Muscat is coordinating with Omani authorities to locate the missing sailors. Indian officials did not identify who was responsible for the October 11, 2026, strikes.

In Iraq, Reuters reported that a drone struck a camp belonging to an Iranian Kurdish opposition group in Koya, east of Erbil. While the Kurdistan-based website Rudaw published video of a drone in the sky over Koya, it stated it was not yet clear if a target had been hit, and no casualties were immediately reported. No responsibility for the strike in Koya has been established. In Iran, Mohsen Rezaei claimed that the US Central Command, with assistance from the United Arab Emirates military, has been using smaller vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers in a shuttle system. Rezaei asserted that Iran had been striking five or six participating vessels nightly for weeks and stated that this shuttle system is now an explicit target for Tehran.

results.sourceTitle: Bangladesh signs $335.78m Chinese loan for Mongla port modernisation | The Daily Star

card.headline: Bangladesh signs $335.78 million Chinese loan to modernise Mongla Port

pages.text: Bangladesh signed a $335.78 million loan agreement with China’s Export-Import (EXIM) Bank on October 12, 2026, to expand and modernise Mongla Port. The project aims to upgrade the port's infrastructure through the construction of two container terminals equipped with modern machinery, a container yard, a container delivery yard, and a cargo handling yard. According to a press release from the Economic Relations Division (ERD) of the Ministry of Finance, the loan is valued at RMB 2.404 billion or Tk 3,592.90 crore.

The Chinese government is providing concessional financing for the modernisation at a 2% interest rate. The loan includes a 20-year repayment period, which features a five-year grace period. Alia Meher, joint secretary of the ERD, signed the agreement for the Bangladesh government, while Fengjun Tian, assistant general manager of China’s EXIM Bank, signed on behalf of the Chinese side.

results.sourceTitle: Hackers force French supermarket fridges to heat up to 50C in ‘unprecedented’ cyber-attack

card.headline: Hackers force French supermarket fridges to heat up to 50C in unprecedented cyber-attack

pages.text: Hackers forced the temperature of refrigerators and freezers in hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50C (122F) overnight, causing food spoilage and fires at several hundred stores. The large-scale attack affected major food retailers across France, including Intermarché, Coopérative U, E.Leclerc, Carrefour, and Monoprix. Intermarché owner Les Mousquetaires reported that approximately 150 of its stores had fridges heated to 50C for six hours, resulting in the disposal of all affected food to prevent health risks. Intermarché CEO Thierry Cotillard told BFM TV the attack could represent losses of tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day. The Paris prosecutor’s office confirmed the attack was affecting connected refrigerators and has opened an investigation to identify victims and establish links to reported food losses and fires. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has instructed the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) to investigate the incident.

The attack targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss, which allows retailers to manage cold units remotely via the internet. According to a source close to the Prime Minister, ANSSI identified a vulnerability in the software supplied by the company. Danfoss stated that the affected equipment consisted of older, legacy models—specifically its AK-SM800 and AK-SC355 fridge regulator systems—which no longer receive security updates. The firm noted it had long advised businesses to keep supported systems up to date. While the full scale of the impact is unclear, individual chain reports suggest approximately 400 stores were affected out of roughly 15,000 in France. Carrefour reported 80 of its 6,000 stores were hit, and Monoprix stated 5% of its 400-plus stores were affected. The attack may not be confined to France; Felix Aime, a senior cyber threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia Threat Detection and Research, said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany, and Belgium had also been affected. Additionally, Dutch supermarket operator Ahold Delhaize reported dealing with a security issue in its network.

results.sourceTitle: NATO commander says the alliance does not want war but is 'ready to fight tonight'

card.headline: NATO Supreme Allied Commander says alliance is 'ready to fight tonight' if attacked

pages.text: NATO's Supreme Allied Commander U.S., General Alexus Grynkewich, stated in Warsaw, Poland, that the alliance is prepared to respond immediately to an attack. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, Grynkewich outlined a military blueprint he called a “Theory of Victory,” which aims to deter Russia by signaling that any aggression would be met with force. While Grynkewich said he does not believe a conflict is imminent or inevitable, he emphasized that preparing for war is a way to preserve peace and maintain communication to resolve misunderstandings. This stance comes as senior European officials and intelligence services warn that Russia may be planning to test NATO defenses through increased covert attacks or a limited military incursion following recent sabotage incidents across the continent, such as an arson attack on an Estonian defense company and a failed attempt to attack a Ukrainian aircraft at a German airport.

Grynkewich's “Theory of Victory” describes a three-part military response to an invasion of NATO territory. First, the alliance would use combined land, sea, and air forces to block an initial attack and prevent Moscow from seizing territory. If the attack persists, the second phase involves using sensors, autonomous systems, and other capabilities to blunt the assault and prevent enemy advances. If required, the final phase would use highly effective precision munitions and unmanned systems to break the enemy's operational war-fighting system, including the forces and everything that supports, sustains, and controls them. Grynkewich noted that this plan accounts for scenarios where U.S. forces might be engaged elsewhere, stating that the alliance must be able to defend itself regardless of U.S. availability.

The commander's remarks arrive amid discussions regarding the level of U.S. commitment to the 32-member alliance. While Grynkewich argued that no one should question the United States' commitment, he noted that providing troops is ultimately a political decision. U.S. ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker stated in Warsaw that Europe ranks fourth among Washington’s strategic concerns, and the Pentagon has already cut contributions to NATO crisis forces, with a review of U.S. forces in Europe expected by the end of the year. Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said the theory laid out by Grynkewich will send a strong message to adversaries regarding the alliance's intent to defend itself.

results.sourceTitle: Israeli army enters Syria’s Quneitra countryside, blocks construction work

card.headline: Israeli army enters Quneitra countryside and blocks construction in Syria

pages.text: Israeli army forces entered southwestern Quneitra Governorate in Syria, blocking local residents from digging foundations for construction work, according to state-run Alikhbariah TV. The broadcaster reported that six Israeli military vehicles advanced south of the town of Al-Rafid in the Quneitra countryside. In a separate incident, Alikhbariah reported that Israeli forces blew up an abandoned military barracks at Tal Harboun near the town of Beit Jinn in the western Damascus countryside. Israel has expanded its military operations in Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime on Dec. 8, 2024, with forces advancing into the demilitarized buffer zone in the occupied Golan Heights and nearby positions. Israel states its actions are driven by security considerations to prevent attacks on Israeli communities.

Syria has demanded that Israel withdraw from occupied territories, reaffirming its commitment to a 1974 disengagement agreement. Damascus has repeatedly called Israeli actions illegal under international law and urged the international community to help secure a full withdrawal. These incursions follow a reported pattern of Israeli military operations in southern Syria, including raids, arrests, and shelling. On Oct. 10, 2026, Syrian media reported an incursion into Al-Mushayrifah village in Quneitra Governorate and along the road to Durbul in the Damascus countryside, where Israeli forces searched vehicles, homes, and pedestrians. Additionally, Syria’s state-run news agency SANA reported that Israeli forces entered a valley near the village of Abidin in southern Syria, preventing farmers from working their land. SANA reported that three military vehicles advanced into the Yarmouk Basin in western Daraa Governorate before withdrawing toward Jamla and returning to occupied territory through the Tal Abu Al-Ghaithar gate. The reporter also noted an Israeli soldier damaged a farmer’s motorcycle during the incursion.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Turk, has expressed concern regarding the continuing toll on civilians. Open-source monitoring recorded approximately 280 incidents involving armed Israeli incursions in September, the highest monthly total since the start of the year. Reported actions included intimidation, harassment, arbitrary detention, movement restrictions, destruction of livelihoods, and raids on homes. On Oct. 7, 2026, the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) received reports that Israeli forces shot and temporarily detained a farmer with a disability during an incursion into Jubbata Al-Khashab in northern Quneitra. According to those reports, the farmer attempted to leave the area because he was frightened by the presence of soldiers; Israeli forces then shot him in the leg and detained him while he was bleeding. The farmer was released approximately 90 minutes later and taken by Syrian Civil Defense personnel to Al-Golan Hospital in Quneitra for surgery and treatment, according to OCHA.

results.sourceTitle: DP World Chattogram Port Deal | DP World to operate Ctg port’s New Mooring Container Terminal | The Daily Star

card.headline: Bangladesh signs 15-year deal with DP World to operate Chattogram port terminal

pages.text: Bangladesh signed a 15-year concession agreement on October 11, 2026, with UAE-based DP World to operate and maintain the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) and its overflow container yard at Chattogram port. The agreement was signed at the Chattogram Port Authority (CPA) headquarters by CPA Chairman Rear Admiral S M Moniruzzaman and DP World chairman Essa Kazim. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, acted as the transaction adviser for the deal. This concession agreement allows a private entity to manage port infrastructure under a public-private partnership framework, a process that began in 2019 but faced delays due to opposition and a workers' strike.

results.sourceTitle: Bangladesh, WB, IMF reach policy consensus on reforms, govt focuses on investment | The Business Standard

card.headline: Bangladesh reaches broad policy alignment with World Bank and IMF on economic reforms

pages.text: Bangladesh has reached broad policy alignment with the World Bank (WB) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) regarding key economic reforms, according to Prof Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, the Adviser to the Prime Minister on Finance and Planning. Speaking to journalists on October 12, 2026, ahead of the 2026 Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group in Thailand, Titumir stated the alignment focuses on restoring stability, strengthening banking sector discipline, increasing tax revenue, and creating employment. This consensus aims to support a five-year economic strategy designed to recover and rebuild the economy. While the government's priorities align with the reform proposals of the WB and IMF, Titumir emphasized that the government will retain ownership of the reform agenda and responsibility for its implementation.

The government's recovery and reconstruction strategy includes several major priorities: increasing domestic and foreign investment, reopening closed factories, expanding social protection, and addressing rising energy costs. Titumir noted that the public expects increased spending on social protection, employment generation through industrialization, and higher tax collection relative to GDP. Regarding energy, Titumir said the government discussed with the World Bank the financial pressure on the energy sector caused by the Middle East conflict that began on 28 February. He stated the government has refrained from fully adjusting domestic energy prices to international market levels to limit the burden on consumers. To support poor households, the present government is planning programs such as the Family Card. Titumir also referenced a recent World Bank report stating that poverty increased during the previous government's tenure.

The initiative is part of the bank's activities marking its 40th anniversary in Africa and serves as the culmination of its three-year Transforming Africa Through Education programme, themed “Building Tomorrow’s Skills Today.” The project is part of Ecobank Day, the Ecobank Group’s annual flagship corporate social responsibility programme observed across its 33 affiliate countries.

results.sourceTitle: B.C. man reunited with beloved flute, 5 years after it floated away down a Yukon river

card.headline: B.C. man reunited with flute found in Yukon river gear barrel

pages.text: Jun Takahashi, a resident of Salt Spring Island, B.C., has been reunited with a flute he purchased in Japan years ago after it was discovered in a waterproof canoe barrel near the confluence of remote rivers in the Yukon. Takahashi recognized the instrument immediately after seeing a social media post featuring a photograph of the flute in a case among other items, including clothes and a sleeping bag.

The gear was found by Colin Abbott, who posted the photo to a Yukon paddling group page. Abbott asked if anyone had lost gear dumped in the Yukon's Kathleen River in the last couple of years. The blue, waterproof barrel containing the camping gear had been found near the confluence of two remote rivers.

Takahashi had used the flute during many travels and found it ideal for remote canoe trips in the Yukon because it could be easily stored inside a waterproof barrel. He noted that he enjoys playing the instrument in wild, open spaces where he will not disturb others.

results.sourceTitle: Olivia Chow pitches school food program expansion, critics question how she'll pay for it

card.headline: Olivia Chow proposes expanding Toronto school food program to include lunches

pages.text: Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow has pledged to create a citywide universal student nutrition program if re-elected, expanding the current system to provide lunches in addition to midday snacks. Chow stated during a debate in Scarborough that the expansion would serve as an affordability measure, potentially saving the average family $1,800 a year. The current program, which receives $32 million in city contributions, serves approximately 330,000 students every day. Chow said the expansion would be phased in by 2030 through collaboration with private donors and other levels of government, though she did not specify the total cost to taxpayers.

Chow's main mayoral challenger, Councillor Brad Bradford, expressed support for the idea but questioned the lack of a funding plan. Bradford noted that there is currently no national or provincial program for such a lunch initiative. Chow responded by stating she could bring other levels of government onside, arguing that leadership and the ambition to ensure no child is hungry in school are necessary to move the plan forward.

results.sourceTitle: No trader will be evicted from Aboabo Market after redevelopment – Mahama Ayariga assures traders

card.headline: Ghanaian Minister assures Aboabo Market traders no evictions will occur during redevelopment

pages.text: Mahama Ayariga, the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, has assured traders at the Aboabo Market in Tamale, Ghana, that no one will be evicted as plans proceed to redevelop the facility. The assurance follows agitation among traders regarding rumors that they would be evacuated to make way for the redevelopment project. During a tour of the market on October 12, Ayariga stated that the government intends to improve existing infrastructure and expand capacity to accommodate more traders rather than displacing current operators. He said, “We are not here to sack anybody. We have no plans of sacking anybody. We are here to develop what you are already managing so that it can take more people.”

Ayariga provided these remarks while engaging with traders alongside Alhassan Suhuyini, the Deputy Minister for Roads and Highways. The Minister noted that completing existing structures at the market is necessary to prevent the waste of resources already invested in the project. He also stated that the redevelopment is intended to fulfill a commitment made by President John Dramani Mahama during the election campaign.

results.sourceTitle: Wasauksing First Nation works to bring back wild rice — and youth are at the centre of efforts - MBC Radio

card.headline: Wasauksing First Nation partners to restore manoomin habitats

pages.text: Wasauksing First Nation partnered with the Anishinabek/Ontario Fisheries Resource Centre (A/OFRC) this summer to assess the health and potential of manoomin (wild rice) habitats within the community in Canada. The project aims to restore a food source central to Anishinaabe culture, identity, and food sovereignty. In spring 2026, Wasauksing submitted a proposal to the A/OFRC to support the revival of manoomin beds by combining scientific expertise and modern tools with local community knowledge. For Wasauksing’s Lands and Resources Office, the initiative seeks to achieve more than ecological recovery; it aims to restore community well-being, self-determination, and the ability to manage and harvest traditional foods.

The restoration efforts include reclaiming cultural practices and traditional knowledge to deepen community connections to water, land, and identity. To support this, Wasauksing visited communities such as Alderville to learn from Elders like Jeff Beaver, whose community has operated a wild rice reintroduction project since the 1990s. Gabrielle Perugini, the A/OFRC’s lead fisheries biologist, stated that the organization's knowledge and the possibility of such restoration projects stem from knowledge keepers like Beaver. During the summer, youth from the community spent one week working with the A/OFRC team to explore local waters, learn the history of manoomin in their territory, and gain hands-on experience monitoring and surveying identified sites. This fieldwork included using equipment to measure water quality and turbidity at potential manoomin sites.

results.sourceTitle: Fisher River Cree Nation students hunt for higher learning through land-based program

card.headline: Fisher River Cree Nation students harvest more than 500 kilograms of moose meat through land-based education program

pages.text: Eight students from Fisher River High School returned to Fisher River Cree Nation on October 9, 2026, with more than 500 kilograms of fresh moose meat following a five-day hunting trip. The group harvested four bull moose during the excursion to Moose Mountain Provincial Park in southeast Saskatchewan. 18-year-old Aidan Traverse, who participated in the trip, intends to share the harvest with the community in Fisher River, a First Nation located in Manitoba's Interlake region approximately 175 kilometres north of Winnipeg.

The trip was part of a land-based education program offered through Fisher River High School. This approach to learning focuses on emotional, spiritual, and cultural health alongside traditional academic success. During the trip, which began on October 5, students traveled nearly 400 kilometres to reach the park. Traverse, who noted it was his first time hunting big game, worked alongside Ashton Amos, a 25-year-old Fisher River outfitter and assistant in the school's land-based education program, to prepare gear including prospector tents, coolers, propane tanks, and fuel.

results.sourceTitle: Govt hands over unused machinery to MBSTU

card.headline: Bangladesh government transfers unused Sonali Bag machinery to MBSTU

pages.text: The Bangladesh government has transferred unused machinery from the Sonali Bag project to Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University (MBSTU) to prevent the deterioration of public assets and support research into jute-based technologies. The Sonali Bag was a project intended to create a biodegradable alternative to plastic using jute cellulose, but it failed to become commercially viable. State Minister for Textiles and Jute Shariful Alam handed the machinery over to the university’s vice-chancellor following a memorandum of understanding signed on October 8 between the Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation (BJMC), the Bangladesh Climate Change Trust, and MBSTU. The machinery is intended to support research into jute cellulose and eco-friendly products, with access available to private researchers and the ministry for research and training purposes.

The Tk 100 crore Sonali Bag project was scrapped on April 29, 2025, following a recommendation from an 11-member technical committee. According to a BJMC statement, the committee found that producing five tonnes of Sonali bags required 40 tonnes of chemicals, which raised environmental concerns. Additionally, the project was deemed commercially unviable because each bag would have needed to sell for Tk 25-40 to cover production costs. Shariful Alam stated that while the project made technological progress, production costs could not be reduced to commercially acceptable levels. He noted that the government is currently working with the environment ministry and other institutions to develop environmentally friendly alternatives to polythene bags.

results.sourceTitle: Seafarer's union official says crews offered big money to transit Strait of Hormuz

card.headline: Crews offered up to five times their salary to transit Strait of Hormuz

pages.text: Merchant sailors are being offered significant financial rewards, including up to five times their regular salary, to transit the Strait of Hormuz due to increasing attacks on shipping vessels in the Middle East. Manoj Yadav, the general secretary of a union representing merchant sailors from India, stated that crews are receiving these large payments to make the crossing because of the heightened danger. Many of the sailors represented by the union work in the Persian Gulf.

The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported that several oil tankers traversing the Strait of Hormuz were attacked recently. Yadav noted that attacks are taking new forms, such as small boats surrounding vessels and firing with guns and RPGs. According to the U.N., nearly a hundred vessels have been hit since the U.S. war with Iran began, resulting in two dozen deaths.

results.sourceTitle: Community action to protect Cambodia’s seas: Interview with commune leader Sorn Srenh

card.headline: Commune leader drives marine conservation efforts in Cambodia’s Koh Sdach archipelago

pages.text: Sorn Srenh, the 38-year-old deputy chief of Koh Sdach commune in Cambodia, is leading grassroots efforts to protect marine biodiversity in the Koh Sdach archipelago. Facing environmental pressures such as climate change, plastic waste, and overfishing, Srenh has worked to balance the economic survival of fishing communities with ecological stewardship. His work involves organizing community capacity and lobbying for stronger local enforcement of fishing regulations to safeguard local livelihoods and marine ecosystems.

To establish a Marine Fisheries Management Area (MFMA)—a community-led conservation zone—Srenh has collaborated with the Cambodian government’s Fisheries Administration and the UK-based NGO Fauna & Flora. Srenh, who studied fishery science at the Royal University of Agriculture in Phnom Penh, stated that his interest in marine ecosystems was sparked by observing NGO activities, including scuba diving, underwater photography, and community capacity building designed to encourage local participation in biodiversity conservation.

results.sourceTitle: High silver prices threaten Lucknow’s famed bridal nagra craft | Longform

card.headline: Rising silver prices reduce demand for traditional bridal nagras in Lucknow, India

pages.text: Soaring silver prices over the past year have caused demand for traditional silver nagras—decorative slip-on shoes—to plummet in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. The decline in sales threatens the livelihood of local craftsmen who have used specialized techniques to produce the footwear since the 1600s. In the Chowk Bazaar, a historic market in Old Lucknow known for wedding shopping and handcrafts, 55-year-old craftsman Azhar Hussain reports that while his tools remain, his customers have disappeared due to the cost of the metal.

The nagra is a distinctive form of footwear that carries significant cultural heritage. Originally made for daily use by the Nawabi, the Muslim rulers of the former kingdom of Awadh, the shoes were once a central part of a nawab’s attire. Nawab Masud Abdullah, a 68-year-old eighth-generation descendant of Nawab Muhammad Ali Shah—the ninth Nawab of Awadh who ruled from 1837 until 1842—stated that the silver nagras represented the culture and heritage of the region. Azhar Hussain, who has worked as a craftsman for three decades, uses a specific manual process to create them: he cuts thin silver sheets into the shoe's outline, sketches floral and leaf motifs, and then rests the metal on heated lac, a soft natural resin that provides cushioning. He uses a hammer and engraving tool to tap designs into the silver before bending the metal around a foot-shaped mould called a furma. The finished silver is then fitted over a base of cardboard, rubber, and velvet, soldered, and polished.

results.sourceTitle: When free speech has a price: Youth voices in Mozambique

card.headline: Youth in Mozambique face risks when speaking on corruption and inequality despite constitutional protections

pages.text: In Mozambique, young people face ongoing risks when speaking publicly about corruption, inequality, police violence, or accountability. While Article 48 of the Constitution of the Republic of Mozambique guarantees freedom of expression, and the Law on the Right to Information No. 34/2014 regulates it, a gap exists between these democratic promises and the daily experiences of the youth. This tension is particularly evident in the capital city of Maputo, where hip-hop has served as a primary medium for urban youth to voice social criticism over the last two decades. This musical movement documents the concerns of a generation that has experienced political democratization and multipartyism since the early 1990s alongside high youth unemployment, economic inequalities, and growing distrust in public institutions led by the ruling FRELIMO party.

Artists and musical groups have used hip-hop to create a language reflecting daily experiences in public and institutional spaces. For example, the group GPRO and the artist Azagaia have utilized musical narratives to address social issues. In the song “O ciclo da Censura” (Cycle of Censorship), Azagaia asks, “Who said that in this country there is freedom of expression?”

results.sourceTitle: Indonesia says it no longer needs forests for rice. What happens to projects underway?

card.headline: Indonesia announces it no longer needs to expand rice cultivation into forest areas

pages.text: Indonesia has announced that it no longer needs to expand rice cultivation into forest areas, claiming the country achieved rice self-sufficiency three years ahead of schedule. Presidential Special Envoy for Climate and Energy Hashim Djojohadikusumo stated in Jakarta that the government sees no further need for the 2 million hectares (4.9 million acres) previously announced for food production in forest areas and forest zones. Presidential Special Envoy for Multilateralism and International Trade Mari Pangestu added that future food and biofuel production would instead be directed toward degraded land. While the announcement suggests a shift away from large-scale projects involving rice and sugarcane plantations in southern Papua—which environmentalists have described as one of the world’s largest deforestation projects—the government has not yet explained what this means for food and energy projects already underway in Papua and Kalimantan.

The announcement has raised questions regarding policy consistency. Less than two weeks before Hashim's statement, the Ministry of Forestry designated approximately 5.67 million hectares (14 million acres) of forest through its 2026 Forest Utilization Direction Map (PAPH) as areas that could be proposed for forest-utilization permits for food security, energy, and forest rehabilitation. Musdalifah Jamal, a campaigner for essential ecosystems with the Indonesian Forum for the Environment (Walhi), told Mongabay that this contradiction shows the government has not yet abandoned a development paradigm that uses forest areas to fulfill food and energy needs. Ministry spokesperson Ristianto Pribadi said the ministry has welcomed the direction of the announcement but noted a distinction must be made between new expansion plans, activities already underway, and increasing production on existing agricultural land. Pribadi stated the ministry cannot yet say if all activities in South Papua and Central Kalimantan will automatically stop, nor can they confirm when they would stop.

results.sourceTitle: ‘We cannot accept foxes as part of our landscape’: the plan to save Australia’s threatened wildlife | Australia news

card.headline: Draft national strategy proposes steps to protect Australian wildlife from invasive foxes

pages.text: A draft national strategy aims to protect Australia's most at-risk native animals from the European red fox, an invasive species that Sarah Legge, a professor at Charles Darwin University, describes as one of the most impactful threats to native mammals. The plan acknowledges that the fox population is too large to be eradicated but outlines methods to curb their predation on vulnerable wildlife. If the federal environment department implements the strategy, it would represent Australia's first updated national effort to mitigate the impact of foxes on native wildlife in nearly two decades. Since the previous plan was released in 2008, Legge notes there have been dramatic advancements in understanding how to combat the species.

The European red fox is estimated to have a population of approximately 1.7 million spread across Australia, from central Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria and South Australia, with populations also thriving in Western Australia. Studies estimate these foxes kill upwards of 367 million native mammals, 111 million birds, and 88 million reptiles annually, along with countless frogs and invertebrates. Legge states that Australia has the worst record of mammal extinctions of any country in the world, with around 40 species lost, citing predation by foxes and cats as the overwhelming cause. The draft plan proposes increased funding for safe havens, such as predator-proof fenced zones and fox-free islands, and calls for legislative harmony and collaboration between state and federal governments.

results.sourceTitle: A headscarf at the school gates: the dispute over hijab and the future of Azerbaijani girls

card.headline: Azerbaijan school hijab restrictions spark protests and student boycotts

pages.text: New government dress code requirements in Azerbaijan have led to schoolgirls being denied entry to lessons and teachers being told to remove their headscarves or resign. The restrictions, which aim to uphold the country's principle of secularism, have triggered protests, student boycotts, and the arrest of 37 people in connection with incidents regarding school uniform compliance, according to the Interior Ministry on October 12, 2026. While the government's amendments do not explicitly name the hijab, they bar clothing that violates the principle of secularism or breaks the integrity of the school uniform. Each school's pedagogical council, which operates under the Ministry of Science and Education, decides whether specific items of clothing meet these rules. Approximately 96 percent of Azerbaijan's population identifies as Muslim, and while the constitution defines the country as secular, it also guarantees religious freedom. The dispute has expanded from students to educators following a Cabinet of Ministers decision on October 6 that requires educators' clothing to comply with the secular nature of education. In Baku and Sumgayit, teachers reported being instructed to uncover their heads or submit resignations. Teacher Zahra Hasanova told Al Jazeera that she felt hurt by the requirement, stating that the hijab is a personal choice. The state-run Azerbaijani Press Agency (APA) stated the amendments aim to ensure a unified dress code and that teachers should reflect professional standards to benefit a school's public reputation.

The restrictions have resulted in visible confrontations at school gates. Social media videos have shown schoolgirls in headscarves being turned away in tears at schools in Sumgayit, the southern Jalilabad district, and the Baku settlement of Khokhmeli. In response, students at School No. 322 and School No. 69 in Baku have staged protests or boycotted classes in solidarity with classmates wearing hijabs. In the village of Mollaoba, in the Masally district, schoolchildren also staged protests. Some parents have expressed that the situation has become a question of access to education; one parent in Sumgayit told AzadlıqRadiosu that their children were not being allowed into school because of their religious beliefs. In Khokhmeli, parents warned they would stop sending their sons to school as well. The legal implications are significant: lawyer Akram Hasanov noted that while parents can be penalized for depriving a child of education under Azerbaijan’s Code of Administrative Offenses, the situation is complex if an adolescent independently refuses to attend school because they will not remove a headscarf. Hasanov argued that excluding girls with religious convictions could alienate them from the state. The unrest has also reached the prison system, where journalist Polad Aslanov, serving a 113-year sentence for high treason, launched a hunger strike to protest the restrictions, according to a message posted by his wife, Gulmira Aslanova.

results.sourceTitle: The building blocks of life on Earth have been found around distant stars that are similar to our Solar System | BBC Sky at Night Magazine

card.headline: Organic molecules found in planet-forming discs around distant stars

pages.text: Astrophysicists have identified organic molecules in protoplanetary discs surrounding young stars, suggesting the raw ingredients for life may be common in the dusty environments where planets are born. Using the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) in Chile, Dr. John Ilee, an astrophysicist studying star and planet formation at the University of Leeds, and his colleagues detected these materials in discs approximately the same size as the Solar System. These discs are located between about 300 to 500 lightyears from Earth, meaning the observations show the discs as they appeared 300 to 500 years ago.

A protoplanetary disc is a ring of cosmic material, such as dust and gas, that circles a newborn star. In our own Solar System, such a ring contained solid materials that coalesced through gravity over time to eventually form the planets orbiting the Sun. By studying these discs around other young stars, astronomers aim to analyze the conditions that may have led to the formation of our own Solar System and the potential development of life on Earth. The regions where these specific discs exist are among the closest star-forming regions to our Solar System, providing astronomers with an excellent view.

The detection of these molecules was made possible by the increased observational capability of ALMA. Compared to previous instruments, ALMA combines extremely high sensitivity with high spatial resolution, allowing researchers to detect faint emissions on small scales. This capability was essential for identifying the organic molecules that could point to the building blocks required for the development of organic life.

results.sourceTitle: A record-breaking X-ray burst from a neutron star merger

card.headline: Astronomers attribute 10-minute X-ray burst to colliding neutron stars

pages.text: Astronomers have attributed a mysterious X-ray burst, known as EP250704a, to the collision of two neutron stars. The event began with a half-second gamma-ray burst followed by approximately 10 minutes of X-ray emissions, a duration about 1,200 times longer than the initial gamma-ray spike. This long-lasting X-ray emission caught the attention of researchers, including Eleonora Troja, a member of the Einstein Probe European collaboration, who noted the unusual nature of the data upon seeing it. While neutron-star mergers are typically associated with gamma-ray flashes that fade within two seconds, new research suggests these collisions can also produce X-ray blasts lasting several minutes.

To explain the extended duration of the X-ray burst, the research team suggests the involvement of a magnetar. Magnetars are rapidly spinning neutron stars characterized by the strongest magnetic fields in the universe. The researchers propose that if the remnant of the collision is a magnetar, it could continue bursting for a longer period by dumping its magnetic power into its surroundings, making the explosion brighter and more long-lasting. This process may occur because a collapsing stellar core can spin a resulting neutron star at more than 700 rotations per second and squeeze magnetic field lines together, strengthening the field. The team's interpretation of the event as a merger rests on ruling out a supernova, though the provided data from the VLT or VLA does not describe any positive signs of a merger, such as a kilonova light.

The discovery provides a test case for hundreds of X-ray flashes logged by the Einstein Probe since its 2024 launch, some of which remain unexplained. Neutron-star mergers are significant cosmic events credited with forging elements such as gold, silver, and platinum. The study of EP250704a helps astronomers understand the diverse ways these high-energy collisions can manifest in the universe.

results.sourceTitle: New Jurassic crocodile species had unusually slender teeth, suggesting it fed on shrimp and tiny fish

card.headline: New Jurassic crocodile relative had slender teeth for eating small aquatic prey

pages.text: Scientists have discovered a new species of ancient crocodile relative that lived approximately 170 million years ago. The animal, named Ctenosuchus tenuidens, possessed a long, narrow snout filled with exceptionally thin, needlelike teeth that differ from those of any known close relative. This unique dental structure suggests the creature fed on small aquatic prey, such as tiny fish and crustaceans like fairy shrimp, rather than hunting large animals. Ctenosuchus tenuidens belonged to a group of marine and freshwater reptiles known as thalattosuchians that lived during the age of the dinosaurs. The fossils were recovered from rocks formed in ancient rivers and lakes in the Atlas Mountains of southeastern Morocco.

The discovery was made by researchers from the University of Portsmouth and Hassan II University of Casablanca, Morocco. Lead author Hamzah Imran, from the University of Portsmouth's School of the Environment and Life Sciences, noted that the team initially identified the teeth as small black circles on either side of a long bone in a fossil. After examining the fossils under a microscope and using a scalpel to uncover more of the structures, the researchers realized they were incredibly thin teeth. Published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, the research details how microscopic examination of the teeth's internal structure revealed specialized ridges and close spacing, supporting the conclusion that the species had a highly unusual diet.

results.sourceTitle: Brain entropy during a psychedelic trip tracks later gains in insight and well-being

card.headline: Increased brain entropy during psilocybin trips tracks later gains in well-being

pages.text: Participants who experienced more irregular brain activity during a high dose of psilocybin tended to show the largest gains in well-being one month later, according to a study published in Nature Communications. The research tracked healthy volunteers who had never previously taken a psychedelic to see if the acute disruptions caused by the drug leave enduring marks on the brain. In addition to well-being, the study found improvements in psychological insight and cognitive flexibility—the ability to adapt thinking and switch between different rules or concepts—one month after the dose. While researchers detected possible changes in the brain's white matter, lasting changes in brain function were largely absent.

Psilocybin is the active psychedelic compound found in “magic mushrooms” that works primarily by stimulating a specific type of serotonin receptor in the brain. Some scientists have proposed that this chemical action scrambles normal brain activity into a more flexible, highly disordered state. This concept is central to the “entropic brain” hypothesis, introduced in a 2014 theoretical paper by Robin Carhart-Harris, the senior author of the new study. The hypothesis suggests that psychedelics expand conscious experience by making brain signals more unpredictable, or increasing brain entropy.
